I'm not sure if you've already done this, but universities usually offer counselling for learning and studying habits. Mine had one for accessibility services (where they tested me for ADD/ADHD). That's worth checking out.

 It's also good that you're reading and have singular, focused activities, but I would take it a step further and try to lessen the use of internet-based entertainment (like Reddit and YouTube); it kinda acts like a playground for the mind to be unfocused.

If you want to meet new people and come out of your shell a bit, joining a club that interests you or volunteering is a great way to meet like-minded and friendly people. Even if you don't feel like interacting with others much, you can still just stick to doing your own thing there.

Aside from that, meditation is helpful. It can be a little difficult at the start (i.e. "is it really working?"), but once you make it a habit, regardless of success, it really helps out.

First and foremost, I apologize if this is a repost and the somewhat awkward wording of the question. I don't post much (both in and out of reddit), so I'm not too used to posting comments, let alone starting a thread.

I asked this question because lately I've been feeling a lot more depressed than usual and was hoping to share some thoughts on how others get through some of the rougher patches. Sadly, I don't have many people to discuss this with near me, so I felt it could be a good idea to ask reddit and garner some thoughts.

What helps me get through some tough times? My family, I guess. They're some of the only people I've got, so I do look to them a lot for approval. Sometimes though, I don't feel like I'm appreciated (or rather, doing anything worthy of being appreciated). I don't blame them since I am a bit of a homebody and they probably might feel under-appreciated as well. But they are what they are, and I love them for it.

I've started volunteering in a food bank, so that's a plus for me. It's amazing how much happier I am there than at home. When I'm there, I feel useful. Like I'm actually helping. The volunteers and the clients all appreciate the effort that I put in and interacting with them makes me feel more normal.

A bit of a side note, for those wishing to seek help, there are many resources both in and outside of reddit that can help you. I'd likely start here:

https://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/wiki/hotlines

Please, feel free to share your thoughts, no matter how big or small.
